question: Identify the option that arranges the chronology of Mughal emperors in the correct order. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/07/2021) Shift 1)
options: Jahangir - Shah Jahan - Akbar - Aurangzeb
Akbar - Shah Jahan - Jahangir - Aurangzeb
Akbar - Jahangir - Shah Jahan - Aurangzeb
Akbar - Aurangzeb - Shah Jahan - Jahangir
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akbar - Jahangir - Shah Jahan - Aurangzeb

Explanation:
The correct chronological order of major Mughal emperors is Akbar (1556-1605), Jahangir (1605-1627), Shah Jahan (1628-1658), and Aurangzeb (1658-1707). Akbar strengthened the empire and promoted religious tolerance. Jahangir patronized arts and culture. Shah Jahan's reign saw the construction of the Taj Mahal and other architectural marvels. Aurangzeb expanded the empire but faced rebellions due to his policies. This sequence is crucial for competitive exams.

question: Who among the following laid the foundation of Qutub Minar at Delhi? (RRB JE Electronics (01/09/2019) Shift 2)
options: Mahmud Ghazni
Mohammad Ghori
Qutb-ud-din-Aibak
Iltutmish
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Qutb-ud-din-Aibak

Explanation:
The Qutub Minar in Delhi is the tallest brick minaret in the world. Its foundation was laid by Qutb-ud-din-Aibak in 1192 AD, who was the founder of the Slave Dynasty. He built it to commemorate the victory of Muhammad Ghori and also in memory of the pillar built by Chandragupta. Later, the top two storeys were completed by Iltutmish. The height of the minaret is 73 meters and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Qutub Minar is made of red sandstone and marble.

question: Who wrote 'Ain-i-Akbari'? It is a 16th-century detailed document recording the administration of the Mughal Empire under Emperor Akbar. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (22/02/2021) Shift 1)

solution:

Explanation:

It is the third volume of the Akbarnama, and it records the administration, revenue system, military, judiciary, and social structure of Akbar's reign. It also includes information about Akbar's Navratnas, religious policies, and various provinces. Written in Persian, this 16th-century work is a primary source for understanding the Mughal Empire under Akbar.

question: Who was the founder of the Khilji dynasty? (RPF SI 2018 (11/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Jalaluddin Khilji
Allauddin Khilji
Malik Kafur
Mubarak Shah Khaliji
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jalaluddin Khilji

Explanation:
The Khilji dynasty was the second ruling dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. It was founded by Jalaluddin Khilji in 1290 AD. He murdered Muizuddin Qaiqabad, the last ruler of the Slave dynasty, and seized power. Jalaluddin Khilji was known as a benevolent and kind ruler, but his reign was short. His nephew and son-in-law Alauddin Khilji murdered him in 1296 AD and became the Sultan. The Khilji dynasty ruled from 1290 to 1320 AD. Major rulers of this dynasty include Jalaluddin Khilji, Alauddin Khilji, and Mubarak Shah Khilji. Malik Kafur was a general under Alauddin, not a ruler.

question: The first ruler of Delhi Sultanate was:  (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (18/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Alauddin Khalji
Iltutmish
Balban
Qutb-ud-din Aibak
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Qutb-ud-din Aibak

Explanation:
The Delhi Sultanate was founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1206 AD. He was a slave of Muhammad Ghori and after Ghori's death, he started ruling independently. Aibak ruled from Lahore and later made Delhi the capital. He was the founder of the Slave Dynasty. He began the construction of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and the incomplete Qutb Minar. His reign lasted from 1206 to 1210 AD. He is regarded as the one who laid the foundation of Islamic rule in India.

question: From which Asian country did Ahmad Shah Abdali come to India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Turkey
Afghanistan
Mongolia
Persia
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Afghanistan

Explanation:
Ahmad Shah Abdali, also known as Ahmad Shah Durrani, was the ruler of Afghanistan. He founded the Durrani Empire and launched several invasions into India during the 18th century. The most notable of these was the Third Battle of Panipat (1761), where he defeated the Maratha Empire. Abdali hailed from the Kandahar region of Afghanistan and expanded his power into India following the decline of the Mughal Empire. He is regarded as a symbol of Afghan nationalism and his invasions significantly impacted the political landscape of the Indian subcontinent.

question: Who among the following is known as the first sovereign ruler of the Delhi sultanate? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (02/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Qutb al-Din Aybak
Ghaznavid Sultan Mahmud
Jalal al-Dın Fıruz Khaljı
Shams al-Din Iltutmish
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Shams al-Din Iltutmish

Explanation:
Shams al-Din Iltutmish (r. 1211–1236) is considered the first sovereign ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. Although Qutb al-Din Aybak laid the foundation of the Sultanate, he remained a military general and did not assume the title of Sultan. Iltutmish, after succeeding Aybak, declared himself Sultan and sought recognition from the Caliph of Baghdad, which legitimized his sovereignty. He introduced the silver Tanka coin and strengthened the administration. Mahmud of Ghazni was an invader of India but not a ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. Jalal al-Din Firuz Khalji was the first ruler of the Khalji dynasty, who came much later. Hence, Iltutmish is rightly regarded as the first sovereign ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.

question: What is the dominant form of decoration employed in Sultanate buildings? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 3)
options: Toranas
Amalaka
Arabesque
Kalasha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Arabesque

Explanation:
The dominant form of decoration in Sultanate buildings is Arabesque. Arabesque is a distinctive feature of Islamic art, characterized by geometric and floral designs. Due to the prohibition of depicting humans and animals in Islam, Arabesque developed as an alternative. It consists of interlacing vines, leaves, and flowers, influenced by Turkish and Iranian styles. In Delhi Sultanate monuments like Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, Alai Darwaza, and Qutub Minar, Arabesque is extensively used. Other options like Toranas and Amalaka are associated with Indian temple architecture, while Kalasha is placed on the spire.

question: What was the Diwan-i-Riyasat under Alauddin Khilji? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (22/03/2026) Shift 1)

Department of agriculture
Department controlling markets and prices
Department of royal correspondence
solution:

Explanation:
During his reign, Alauddin Khilji implemented a price control policy. Under this policy, prices of goods were fixed and strict control was maintained over the market. For this purpose, he created a separate department called Diwan-i-Riyasat, headed by Yana Malik. This department was responsible for monitoring the market and prices. Alauddin Khilji fixed the prices of grains, cloth, horses, etc. Shopkeepers were registered and severe punishments were given for violations. This was the first and most effective price control system of its kind in the Delhi Sultanate period.

question: Select the INCORRECT combination of the books and their respective authors. (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Prithiviraj Raso – Chand Bardai
Tughlaq Nama – Abul Fazal
Gita Govinda – Jayadeva Goswami
Baburnama – Babur
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tughlaq Nama – Abul Fazal

Explanation:
The author of Tughlaq Nama is Amir Khusro, not Abul Fazal. Abul Fazal is the author of Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari. Prithviraj Raso was composed by Chand Bardai, a court poet of Prithviraj Chauhan. Gita Govinda is a famous Sanskrit poetic work by Jayadeva Goswami, centered on the love of Radha and Krishna. Baburnama is the autobiography of Babur, written by himself in Turkish and later translated into Persian. Thus, only the combination of Tughlaq Nama is incorrect.

question: After visiting India and learning about Indian culture, Al-Biruni wrote which book? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (18/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Chahar Maqala
Babarnama
Qiran us Sa'dain
Kitab-Ul-Hind
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kitab-Ul-Hind

Explanation:
Al-Biruni (973-1048 AD) was a great Persian scholar, mathematician, and historian. He accompanied Mahmud of Ghazni to India and stayed here for about 13 years. He deeply studied Indian culture, religion, philosophy, science, and society. As a result of this study, he wrote the famous book 'Kitab-Ul-Hind' (or 'Tarikh-Ul-Hind') in Arabic. This book presents a detailed account of India's social, religious, and scientific life. In this text, Al-Biruni shed light on Indian philosophy, astronomy, mathematics, medicine, and customs. This book is considered an important source for understanding medieval Indian history and culture.

question: Which term is used to describe the conflict between the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Palas, and Rashtrakutas over the control of northern India? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (22/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Tripartite
Chakravartin
Dharmayuddha
Mahasangram
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tripartite

Explanation:
The prolonged struggle among the Gurjara-Pratihara, Pala, and Rashtrakuta dynasties for control of northern India is known as the Tripartite struggle. This conflict lasted from the 8th to the 10th century and was primarily over the possession of Kannauj, which was a symbol of imperial power. The Gurjara-Pratiharas ruled western India, the Palas ruled eastern India, and the Rashtrakutas ruled the Deccan. The constant warfare exhausted these kingdoms, weakening northern India and paving the way for invasions by Mahmud of Ghazni. The term "tripartite" refers to the three parties involved in this conflict.

question: What was a major administrative feature in the military governance system of early South Indian kingdoms, such as the Chalukyas and Rashtrakutas? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (27/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Feudatory chiefs were assigned military and administrative duties
Temple authorities directly recruited soldiers for village defence
District leaders were rotated annually by royal decree
Military governance was entirely centralised under the royal council
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Feudatory chiefs were assigned military and administrative duties

Explanation:
A major administrative feature in the military governance system of early South Indian kingdoms like the Chalukyas and Rashtrakutas was the assignment of military and administrative duties to feudatory chiefs. These chiefs, known as 'Mandaleshwar' or 'Rashtrapati', were responsible for tax collection, justice, local peace, and overseeing military campaigns in their territories. They provided military support to the king in exchange for land grants and political autonomy. This system facilitated the expansion of the empire by incorporating local chiefs into governance, leading to decentralization of administration. It was a kind of feudal structure that strengthened the central military rule. Other options, such as recruitment by temple authorities or annual rotation of district leaders, were not key features of these kingdoms. Military governance was not entirely centralized under the royal council; instead, it was decentralized through feudatory chiefs.

☛ Which famous temple was built by the Rashtrakutas? → Kailasa temple (Ellora)

चालुक्य और राष्ट्रकूट जैसे प्रारंभिक दक्षिण भारतीय राज्यों में सैन्य शासन प्रणाली की एक प्रमुख प्रशासनिक विशेषता सामंती प्रमुखों को सैन्य और प्रशासनिक कर्तव्यों का आवंटन था। ये सामंती प्रमुख, जिन्हें 'मंडलेश्वर' या 'राष्ट्रपति' कहा जाता था, अपने अधीन क्षेत्रों में कर संग्रह, न्याय, स्थानीय शांति और सैन्य अभियानों की देखरेख करते थे। वे राजा को सैन्य सहायता प्रदान करते थे और बदले में भू-अनुदान और राजनीतिक स्वायत्तता प्राप्त करते थे। इस प्रणाली ने साम्राज्य के विस्तार को सुगम बनाया, क्योंकि स्थानीय प्रमुखों को शासन में शामिल करके प्रशासन का विकेंद्रीकरण हुआ। यह एक प्रकार का सामंतवादी ढांचा था, जो केंद्रीय सैन्य शासन को सुदृढ़ करता था। अन्य विकल्प जैसे मंदिर प्राधिकारियों द्वारा भर्ती या जिला नेताओं का वार्षिक स्थानांतरण इन राज्यों की प्रमुख विशेषता नहीं थे। केंद्रीकृत सैन्य शासन भी नहीं था, बल्कि विकेंद्रीकरण था।

Preventing Harshavardhana from crossing the Narmada was a testament to Pulakesin II's military superiority. After this battle, Pulakesin II assumed titles like Parameshwara and Dakshinapateshwara. question: The Rashtrakutas were primarily known for which architectural marvel? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (17/03/2026) Shift 3)

Explanation:
The Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I (756-773 CE) built the Kailasa Temple at Ellora, Maharashtra. This temple is a monolithic structure carved out of a single rock and is considered a masterpiece of Indian architecture. The temple is 84 feet high and 154 feet long, aligned north-south, and built in the rathakara style. It took about 8,000 laborers 18 years to complete. The Ellora caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Rashtrakutas also patronized Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu faiths. question: The founder of the Chola empire, Vijayalaya, was the feudatory of which of the following South Indian powers? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (24/03/2026) Shift 2)

solution:

Explanation:

question: In the Chola empire, the tax-free lands donated to Brahmins where they settled were known as ___________. (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (16/03/2026) Shift 2)
options: Mahasabha
Garbhagriha
Valanadu
Agraharam
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Agraharam

Explanation:
In the Chola empire, the tax-free lands donated to Brahmins for their settlement were known as Agraharam. These were villages or plots of land where Brahmins resided and were exempted from taxes. This practice was a significant form of religious endowment, providing social and economic support to the Brahmin community. The Chola rulers actively promoted the development of Agraharams, which helped in fostering education and culture. The other options: Mahasabha was the village assembly, Garbhagriha is the inner sanctum of a temple, and Valanadu was an administrative division.

question_hi: चोल साम्राज्य में, ब्राह्मणों को दान में दी गई कर-मुक्त भूमि, जहाँ वे बस गए थे, __________ के नाम से जानी जाती थी। (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (16/03/2026) Shift 2)

वलनाडु

solution_hi:
